item.title: Mahdi: PM’s UNGA visit highlights Bangladesh’s interests, global opportunities
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s four-day visit to New York for the 81st United Nations General Assembly highlighted Bangladesh’s national interests and sovereignty while presenting the country’s aspirations for partnership, investment, trade and inclusive development before the international community, Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin said on Wednesday.
“During these four working days, the prime minister firmly presented Bangladesh’s interests and potential before the world community in different areas, while highlighting the country’s sovereignty and independence,” he said at a press conference at the Karabi Hall of the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon.
Mahdi, also spokesperson to the Prime Minister's Office, said the prime minister took part in 30 official programs during his four-day stay in New York, held bilateral meetings with 11 countries and delivered six speeches at different events besides his main address to the General Debate of the 81st UNGA.
He said the prime minister travelled with a 35-member official delegation, including 15 ministers, state ministers, advisers and special assistants.
Members of the delegation attended around 50 additional meetings during the visit, taking the total number of bilateral and multilateral engagements involving Bangladesh’s representatives to more than 80, Mahdi said.
A smaller team has also travelled to California to pursue cooperation with the US technology industry and academia, he added.
Of the prime minister’s 30 official programs, eight were directly related to the United Nations, including the opening of the 81st UNGA, his General Debate address, a breakfast hosted by UN Secretary-General António Guterres, a reception hosted by US President Donald Trump and four high-level side events.
In his maiden UNGA address, the prime minister presented Bangladesh’s priorities on democracy, accountability, transparency, inclusive development, human rights, rule of law, freedom of expression, economic recovery, employment, health, education, technology and climate action.
He outlined the government’s three-R strategy of recovery, restoration and reconstruction and presented initiatives including the Family Card, Farmer Card, Health Card and a proposed Universal Card.
Mahdi said the prime minister also highlighted the country’s plans to develop human resources, create employment, promote entrepreneurship and expand the use of artificial intelligence and robotics.
“He presented a roadmap for a prosperous, self-reliant and welfare-oriented Bangladesh, where the benefits of development reach people across all sections of society,” Mahdi said.
Climate action was another major focus of the visit. At high-level meetings on climate action and just transition and sea-level rise, the prime minister presented Bangladesh’s plans to plant 250 million trees over five years, excavate 20,000 kilometres of canals, implement the Teesta Master Plan and Padma Barrage projects, expand solar and renewable energy and promote green industries, he said.
The prime minister also proposed stronger international action on climate resilience, climate finance and the Loss and Damage Fund.
Mahdi said at a Bangladesh-co-organized high-level event on midwifery and maternal health, the prime minister outlined plans to recruit 100,000 healthcare workers, with women expected to make up 80% of the new recruits, and stressed expanding healthcare access from the union level to upazila, district and divisional levels.
The Rohingya crisis also received particular attention, he said, adding that at a high-level side event co-convened by Bangladesh and The Gambia, the prime minister presented a five-point roadmap for early, safe, voluntary, dignified and sustainable repatriation, alongside measures on humanitarian support, rights and security, justice and accountability, and regional and international cooperation.
Mahdi said the roadmap was positively received by the stakeholders attending the event and could serve as a framework for future discussions.
“Myanmar was not directly engaged on that platform, but we spoke with all the stakeholders present at the UN event. The five-point roadmap presented by the prime minister was broadly accepted. Based on future conversations with the UN and other stakeholders, Bangladesh’s engagement will be strengthened, and the roadmap may serve as an important framework for those discussions,” he said.
On bilateral diplomacy, Mahdi said the prime minister’s meetings with 11 countries covered equality, fairness, dignity, people-to-people relations, health, education, travel, manpower exports, trade and investment.
Discussions with Middle Eastern countries placed particular emphasis on manpower exports, trade and investment, while meetings with South Asian countries focused on regional cooperation, stability and democracy, he said.
He said the prime minister also held meetings with the UN Secretary-General, UN officials, the World Bank president, Gates Foundation representatives, International Peace Institute officials and leading Wall Street investors.
Mahdi said the UN Secretary-General congratulated the prime minister on his electoral victory and appreciated Bangladesh’s contribution to UN peacekeeping and its humanitarian role in hosting the Rohingyas.
The World Bank discussed technical and financial support for Bangladesh’s development programs, while talks with around 25 leading Wall Street investors focused on investment in Bangladesh’s financial sector and the introduction of bonds and other financial instruments, he said.
The adviser said the prime minister also met Boeing representatives against the backdrop of the government’s agreement to purchase 11 aircraft.
He said prime minister’s spouse, Dr Zubaida Rahman, also had a busy schedule, participating in eight programs and delivering three speeches. She attended the Women Leaders platform, the First Spouses’ Dialogue, the midwifery event, a program hosted by US First Lady Melania Trump and the UN Secretary-General’s breakfast, among others, he added.
Asked what message Bangladesh conveyed to the international community, Mahdi said the prime minister presented the country’s democratic journey and plans for a self-reliant, modern and welfare-oriented state, while also outlining Bangladesh’s role in promoting global peace.
“He (PM) made it clear that Bangladesh wants bilateral and multilateral cooperation based on equality, fairness, mutual interest and dignity, while ensuring the rule of law, human rights and freedom of expression,” said Mahdi.
He said the prime minister’s UNGA visit was ultimately aimed at presenting Bangladesh’s interests and potential while expanding opportunities for international partnership.
“Everywhere the prime minister went, Bangladesh’s national interests and sovereignty remained at the forefront. We want partnership, investment and trade with different countries so that we can ensure self-reliance, economic strength and inclusive development,” he said.
Prime Minister’s Press Secretary AAM Saleh Shibly, Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Ruman, Prime Minister’s Speech Writer Mahfuzur Rahman, Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu, Deputy Press Secretary Md Suzauddhowla (Sujan Mahmud), Assistant Press Secretary Shahriar Pamir and Assistant Press Secretary KM Nazmul Haque were present at the press conference.

item.title: Swapon: Govt pledges policy support for young AI researchers
item.description:
The government has pledged policy support for young researchers working in artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors and robotics, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's political adviser Zahir Uddin Swapons has said.
He made the comment as the chief guest at the project presentation and closing ceremony of "Nippon AI Dojo 2026" at the University of Asia Pacific (UAP) auditorium in Dhaka.
He urged young technologists to deepen their research and develop AI tools, platforms, datasets and programs tailored to Bangladesh’s practical needs while also pursuing world-class technologies.
“Foreign AI tools alone will not be enough for Bangladesh,” Swapon said, highlighting challenges related to electricity generation, computing and graphics processing unit (GPU) capacity, and the availability of Bengali-language datasets.
He said young researchers should also examine the electricity demand and natural-resource requirements associated with developing and operating AI technologies.
Swapon said the prime minister had announced policy support for research and development in robotics, semiconductors and AI.
However, he said experts and researchers should provide the government with clear roadmaps and policy options to help shape appropriate measures.
The political adviser also praised Japan’s partnership in developing young people’s skills in advanced technologies and said such initiatives could help strengthen Bangladesh’s technological capacity.
The event was jointly organized by UAP, Japan-based Chowa Giken Corporation and AI Samurai Japan.
Japanese Ambassador to Bangladesh Saida Shin-ichi attended the program as the guest of honour.
Speakers at the event included Sayed Abdullah, UAP Acting Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Abu Sayeed M Ahmed and UAP Board of Trustees Chairman KM Mozibul Hoque.
The program was chaired by UAP Board of Trustees member Qayum Reza Chowdhury.
Trainees from UAP, BRAC University and North South University presented their AI projects at the event and received certificates upon completion of the program.
The projects explored applications of AI in areas including agriculture, healthcare, education, manufacturing and freelancing.
The organisers, faculty members, researchers and participants also attended the closing ceremony.

item.title: Health minister: Doctors continue serving despite limitations
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain has said doctors across Bangladesh are continuing to provide services day and night despite various limitations .
He made the comments while speaking as the chief guest at a discussion held on Wednesday after inaugurating the upward expansion of the National Institute of Ear, Nose and Throat (ENT) and its upgradation to a 250-bed facility in Tejgaon, Dhaka.
The health minister said various initiatives are being taken to enhance the skills of doctors and provide them with opportunities to gain international experience.
He said efforts are underway to expand opportunities for higher training and fellowships for doctors through cooperation with China, Pakistan and various international organizations.
The minister also urged the media and journalists to understand the realities and challenges faced by doctors in carrying out their duties.
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain inaugurates the expansion of the National Institute of Ear, Nose and Throat and its upgrade to a 250-bed facility in Tejgaon, Dhaka, on Wednesday, September 30, 2026. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
He advised health service providers to maintain a positive attitude towards addressing any shortcomings or mistakes through constructive discussions in the media.
Sakhawat Husain said it is impossible to build a prosperous economy without a healthy and strong population.
“Therefore, everyone involved must be more sincere in ensuring healthcare for people in remote and marginalized communities while upholding the dignity of the medical profession,” he said.
Director of the National Institute of Ear, Nose and Throat Professor Dr Hasan Zafar presided over the discussion.
Dr Zahirul Islam Shakil, secretary general of the Doctors Association of Bangladesh (DAB), Professor Dr AKM Azizul Haque, chairman of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital, and DAB President Professor Dr Harun Al Rashid also spoke at the event.

item.title: Natore rape convict makes threats after release on bail
item.description:
Firoz Islam, a rape convict sentenced to life imprisonment in a case involving a 15-year-old SSC examinee, made a threatening speech in Nazirpur of Gurudaspur upazila in Natore after being released on bail on appeal on Tuesday night.
Firoz, 48, was released from Rajshahi Jail following a higher court order granting him bail. He later held a meeting with local people in Nazirpur, where he made the remarks.
Speaking at the meeting, Firoz said: “So, I have been sentenced. Do you have any idea how far corruption has gone? A case was filed against me. If four people’s testimony can get me life imprisonment, then there are several thousand people here, and they are testifying about what the opponents have done. There will be a trial. But the trial has already begun. I promise you, their trial will take place on this soil of Nazirpur.”
Firoz did not specify whom he was referring to in his remarks. However, it has been reported locally that the father of the victim and plaintiff in the case has already been threatened, reports Bangla Tribune.
The plaintiff said: “I have been threatened with death since the accused was released on bail. He also threatened to carry out the trial on the soil of Nazirpur. We are living in fear with our family. I have informed the police at the police station.”
Firoz is a former headteacher of Nazirpur Mariam Memorial Girls’ High School in Gurudaspur upazila. He is the son of Golam Mostofa of Daulatpur village in Nazirpur and a former senior vice-president of Gurudaspur upazila BNP.
He was accused of abducting and confining a student of the same school and raping her. He also recorded a video of the incident.
Rajshahi Speedy Trial Tribunal Judge Md Mahiduzzaman convicted Firoz and delivered the verdict under two separate sections on November 11, 2025.
According to police and local sources, Firoz’s supporters welcomed him with flower garlands at the main gate of Rajshahi Jail on Tuesday after arriving in a convoy of more than 200 vehicles.
He later held a meeting in Nazirpur at night attended by several hundred people, where he made various remarks. A video of his speech has since spread on Facebook, prompting criticism.
Speedy Trial Tribunal Public Prosecutor Munshi Abul Kalam Azad said the court sentenced Firoz to life imprisonment after finding him guilty of rape and handed him 10 years of rigorous imprisonment under a separate section for abduction.
He said the victim’s family had been satisfied with the court’s verdict but became fearful after Firoz secured bail on appeal.
The girl’s father said: “Since the case was filed until the verdict, Firoz threatened us in various ways with people at different times over 3 years. He tried to persuade us to reach a settlement by offering money. But thinking about my daughter’s and family’s honor, I continued the case despite all the difficulties.”
He added: “We were satisfied with the verdict of the Rajshahi Speedy Trial Tribunal. But after serving 11 months in jail, the accused obtained bail from the Appellate Division. He came out and threatened to carry out the trial. We are now facing serious security concerns.”
According to the case records, the student from a village in Gurudaspur upazila studied at Nazirpur Mariam Memorial Girls’ High School.
On October 1, 2022, when she went to the school to sit for her SSC practical examination, Firoz allegedly took her away in a microbus from in front of the school gate in public, reports Bangla Tribune.
He later allegedly took her to a residential hotel in Rajshahi and sexually violated her. The girl’s father subsequently filed a rape case with Gurudaspur police station against Firoz and his two brothers.
On October 11 that year at around 12:15am, then Rapid Action Battalion-5 (RAB-5) arrested Firoz from a residential hotel in Taktitala of Kaliakair upazila in Gazipur.
Public Prosecutor Munshi Abul Kalam Azad said: “The verdict in the case was scheduled for November 11, 2025. Before that, when Firoz appeared before the court on the date fixed for November 27, the court cancelled his bail and ordered that he be sent to jail. The accused were produced before the court when the verdict was delivered.”
He said: “The final report submitted by the police, witness testimonies and the video of the rape proved two offences against Firoz. The judge then convicted him and sentenced him to life imprisonment under the rape section and 10 years of rigorous imprisonment under another section for abduction. Police later took Firoz to jail. The other two accused were acquitted.”
Gurudaspur police station Officer-in-Charge Abdul Hannan said: “If the plaintiff in the rape case is unlawfully threatened, legal action will be taken subject to a complaint.”

item.title: One third of world population exposed to harmful air pollution
item.description:
Heatwaves and wildfires combined with human-caused emissions this year combined to expose one third of the world’s population to extremely high levels of ozone pollution, a European Union report said on Wednesday.
In a new analysis covering the first eight months of 2026, the European Union’s Copernicus Climate Atmosphere Monitoring Service (Cams) highlighted the close relationship between climate change and air pollution.
When heat and sunlight react with airborne emissions from wildfires, vehicles and industry, they create ground-level ozone pollution, which can damage lung tissue, cause breathing problems, trigger asthma attacks and lead to other health issues.
Despite progress in cutting the most harmful air pollutants in recent decades, ozone has proved more difficult to tackle as climate change fuels the conditions that favor its formation.
This year’s ozone pollution was driven in part by record-breaking heatwaves and wildfires that seared Europe and North America and sent smoke well beyond their borders.
Indonesia has experienced major wildfires, while the warming El Nino weather pattern, which started in June and is due to peak later this year, could drive more fires in southeast Asia, according to the analysis.
“Air pollution does not stop at borders. It can travel thousands of kilometers, crossing continents and oceans and affecting air quality far from its source,” Cams director Laurence Rouil said in the Atmosphere Watch report.
Cams uses satellite data and computer models to track air pollution and wildfires.
The report found that 34% of the global population was exposed to “extremely poor” air quality between January 1 and September 15, meaning concentrations of ozone were well above the World Health Organization’s exposure guidance.
The WHO’s guideline sets 100 micrograms of ozone per cubic meter as the maximum recommended level of exposure, averaged over eight hours.
Another 17% of the world breathed “very poor” air, while 5% was exposed to “good” levels of ozone.
Asia has the highest rate of exposure to ozone pollution, with 53% of its population breathing “extremely poor” air. Another 22% was exposed to “very poor” ozone.
The continent’s widespread emissions are driven by industrialization, economic development and transport, as well as wildfires and the burning of agricultural residue.
New Delhi, Dhaka, Chinese megalopolis Chongqing and Pakistan’s Lahore were among cities whose ozone levels were “extremely poor.”
Two thirds of the population in North America and 45% in Europe were exposed to “poor” or “very poor” air quality.
EU regulation has been effective in reducing emissions from air pollutants, except for ozone, the report said.
Ozone pollution is linked to 60,000 premature deaths per year in Europe, Ian Marnane, an official at the European Environment Agency, told a media briefing.
Ozone levels in North America also remained “relatively unchanged” despite ambitious emissions reduction policies, the report said.
Smoke from forest fires, crop burning and cooking are significant contributors to Africa’s air pollution while Saharan dust travels as far as Europe.
8% of Africa’s population endured “extremely poor” air quality this year. It was “very poor” or “poor” for 19% of the continent.
Ozone levels were very high in the Brazilian city of Sao Paulo and extremely elevated in Rio de Janeiro but the air quality was “good” or “fair” for 81% of South America’s population.
One bright spot was Oceania, including Australia and New Zealand, where 66% of the population enjoyed “good” ozone levels and 34% lived under “fair” conditions.

item.title: ICB’s golden jubilee: From five decades of trust to a new era of capacity
item.description:
Investment Corporation of Bangladesh (ICB) is completing five decades of its journey in Bangladesh’s investment and capital market landscape.
Established on October 1, 1976, the state-owned financial institution has played an important role in transforming savings into investment, providing capital to industry and business through bridge financing, and contributing to the development of the capital market by creating demand and supply for listed securities.
Established in continuation of the journey of democratic, economic and institutional development that began during the tenure of president Ziaur Rahman with national interest placed at the forefront, ICB has gradually expanded its role in response to the changing needs of the country’s economy.
Its contribution has gone beyond direct participation in the capital market. In 1977, ICB introduced investment schemes and margin lending, followed by the country’s first mutual fund in 1980 and a unit fund in 1981.
Over the years, these initiatives have helped create investment opportunities and channels for mobilizing long-term capital.
According to institutional data, ICB’s direct investment stands at around Tk8,900 crore, while indirect investment through various schemes and mutual funds is approximately Tk27,900 crore.
Around 238 companies have received support through these activities, of which nearly 80 have been listed on the capital market.
The activities have also contributed to the creation of around 20,000 jobs.
The Equity and Entrepreneurship Fund has emerged as another significant initiative.
As of June 30, 2025, Tk1,624.27 crore had been disbursed to 1,039 projects in the agriculture and ICT sectors, contributing to approximately 51,806 direct and indirect employment opportunities.
ICB’s five-decade journey, however, has also involved considerable challenges, including market downturns, high financing costs, liquidity pressures, declining asset values, provisioning shortfalls and maturity mismatches.
The government has already provided Tk1,000 crore to strengthen the corporation’s financial capacity.
As ICB marks its Golden Jubilee, the challenge is not merely to celebrate its past achievements but to prepare the institution for the economic needs of tomorrow’s Bangladesh.
Expanding into areas such as Alternative Investment Funds, ETFs, Sukuk, corporate bonds, SIP/CIP, REITs and infrastructure financing could open new avenues for long-term capital mobilization.
At the same time, stronger investment in technology, skilled human resources, research, risk management, digital finance, data analytics and corporate governance will be crucial.
The Golden Jubilee, therefore, offers an opportunity for ICB to build on five decades of institutional trust and evolve into a more modern, diversified and sustainable institution—capable of turning savings into productive capital and helping shape the markets of Bangladesh’s future.

item.title: Power Ministry, HSBC & Carbon Trust initiate National Energy Study
item.description:
The Power Division under Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, HSBC and The Carbon Trust gathered to initiate the proposed “National Energy Study for Bangladesh”, a study aimed at supporting the country’s long-term energy security and transition towards a more sustainable and resilient energy system.
The meeting was chaired by KM Ali Reza, additional secretary, Renewable Energy Wing, Power Division, and attended by representatives from relevant ministries from the government, HSBC, and the Carbon Trust team.
The study aims to explore practical pathways to building a more affordable, reliable and sustainable energy system.
It will assess Bangladesh's current energy landscape, examine future electricity needs, and evaluate how technologies such as renewable energy, energy storage and other low carbon solutions could support long term economic growth and energy security.
Through analysis, stakeholder engagement and capacity building, the study will help inform future energy planning and provide a roadmap to support Bangladesh's transition to a resilient power sector.
According to the Ministry of Power, the study aims to identify cost efficient clean energy solutions for the Government of Bangladesh and potential pathways to attract foreign direct investment.
HSBC is supporting the study by working with governments and public-sector institutions to explore climate and energy transition solutions.
The bank has partnered with The Carbon Trust to support the study and provide training to help execute the plan.
Speaking at the session, KM Ali Reza, additional secretary, Renewable Energy Wing, Power Division, said: “This marks the start of an important study that will explore potential options for Bangladesh’s energy mix for Power generation. We welcome the partnership with the Carbon Trust and HSBC and look forward to identifying practical pathways towards a more affordable, green, reliable and secure Power system”.
Mahbub ur Rahman, chief executive officer, HSBC Bangladesh, said: “Given the current context, where the global energy markets face heightened uncertainty, this National Energy Study on Bangladesh is an important and timely initiative which HSBC is proud to support. As a long-standing partner to Bangladesh, we recognize that energy security is fundamental to the country’s sustained economic growth, competitiveness, and resilience. Through this study, we hope to support the Government of Bangladesh in shaping forward-looking and sustainable energy strategy, while supporting the long-term energy needs of our clients operating in the country.”
Andrew Lever, director, energy transition, Carbon Trust, said: “Bringing our global expertise across fossil transition, grid modernization and renewable integration we are looking forward to supporting the Government of Bangladesh in identifying pathways towards a prosperous, resilient and decarbonized energy future.”
The Carbon Trust is a global team of climate experts driven by the mission to accelerate the transition to a prosperous, resilient, low-carbon future.
It has more than 25 years’ experience connecting the dots across sectors worldwide, working alongside businesses, governments, public sector bodies, financial institutions and philanthropies.
The proposed National Energy Study forms part of HSBC’s broader approach to supporting key stakeholders in accelerating the transition towards a more resilient future.

item.title: Dinesh Trivedi stresses proper preparations before Tarique-Modi summit
item.description:
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi on Wednesday laid emphasis on proper preparations by both sides before the meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi, noting that there is no benefit in rushing.
“We have to make sure that proper preparations are made because many issues will have to be discussed - trade, commerce, water - many issues. We are very positive about the future,” he told reporters in response to a question.
After a courtesy meeting with Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan, the high commissioner said they have to give both prime ministers a convenient time.
“As far as the prime minister’s visit is concerned, the atmosphere is absolutely positive,” said the Indian envoy, noting that no discussion had been held about the timing or month, but the visit would definitely take place.
He said there would be no issues for which a solution could not be found if the two leaders met and sat together. “See, challenges will be there. If we think there are no challenges - that would be wrong.”
Meanwhile, Indian External Affairs Ministry Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal on Tuesday evening said the two countries have a Joint Rivers Commission and that all matters relating to rivers - including the Ganga Water Treaty and other rivers shared by the two countries - would be discussed under the JRC.
“To also let you know that, at the technical level, meetings on the Ganga Water Treaty have continued to happen,” he told reporters in New Delhi.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Tuesday said Bangladesh and India would overcome their existing challenges through dialogue and discussion, expressing optimism about positive outcomes in the near future and a visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to India.
“Of course, there are some challenges. We are hopeful that we can overcome these challenges through dialogue and discussion. And, of course, you know, at some point, with a conducive environment in place, a visit by the prime minister also… We had a very good discussion,” he told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the afternoon.
Asked about the timing of the visit, he said it would be decided later through mutual discussion.
“So, we will do a visit when the environment is conducive, based on mutual respect,” said the state minister, noting that they had a “very good, cordial and productive” conversation.
On speculation that November could be a possible timeframe, Kobir declined to comment. “There are many rumours, but I do not talk about rumours. I talk about reality, and the reality is that we had a very good meeting today,” he added.
Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi on Tuesday described the overall state of Bangladesh-India relations as “absolutely positive”, saying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to India would take place at a mutually convenient time.
“I am telling you again. Our invitation is open. I don't think there is a need for a hurry. Everything is very positive. But we must give due time,” he told reporters in response to a question at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Bangladesh underscored its commitment to working in a forward-looking and mutually respectful way with India on issues of mutual interest and for the benefit of the people.

item.title: Speakers call for media role in youth participation in reforms
item.description:
Speakers at a roundtable in Dhaka on Wednesday called for a greater role for the media in ensuring meaningful youth participation in Bangladesh’s democratic reform process.
Voices and The Bangladesh Dialogue jointly organized the discussion, titled “Role of Media in Democratic Reform and Decision-Making Processes,” under the “Joining Youth in Effective Engagement in Reform Agendas in Bangladesh (JoYEE)” project.
The discussion focused on how the media can bring young people’s priorities, concerns and recommendations into the policymaking process while promoting participation, accountability and institutional reform.
Referring to the role played by young people in the July 2024 mass uprising, speakers stressed the need for opportunities for them to participate meaningfully in decision-making and the reform process rather than limiting their involvement to consultation or symbolic representation.
The Daily Star Consulting Editor Kamal Ahmed said a vibrant media is essential to a constructive democratic process.
“Young people should continue to raise their demands for reforms and remain vocal in ensuring accountability and responsibility from media institutions and political actors,” he said.
Senior journalist and columnist Sohrab Hassan said the media should play a more active role in bringing young people’s expectations and concerns into broader public discourse.
He said stronger cooperation between young people and the media could help bring their expectations into policymaking and implementation.
Ayesha Kabir, head of the English department at Prothom Alo, said the media can serve as a bridge between young people and the mainstream of democratic reforms.
She stressed the need to present young people’s perspectives objectively and based on evidence while giving greater attention to issues important to the new generation.
In his closing remarks, Voices Executive Director Ahmed Swapan Mahmud said youth participation should not be limited to consultation or symbolic representation.
He said institutional mechanisms were needed to enable young people to influence decision-making, ensure accountability within institutions and play a meaningful role in the reform process.
Editors, sub-editors and young representatives from different media outlets attended the discussion.
Speakers also called for greater participation of women and Indigenous journalists in administrative roles within media organizations, alongside stronger accountability in implementing reforms.
